lang_features.annotations.description: Optional type hints on assignments and function signatures, in the standard Python (PEP 526) form. `thermometer: Thermometer = get_component("thermometer")` documents the variable's type inline; the editor uses the annotation for hover, autocomplete, and Cmd+click navigation. Function params accept the same form (`def f(x: int):`) along with a return annotation (`-> Site:`). Generic shapes work: `xs: list[Site] = []`, `m: dict[str, int] = {}`, `b: Optional[Battery] = None`. Annotations help the editor understand your code. Annotation types are not evaluated and do not check or convert values at runtime. The structural exception is `@dataclass`: annotated class-attribute names become fields used to generate its constructor and other methods.
lang_features.annotations.title: Type Annotations
lang_features.bitwise.description: The `|`, `&`, `^` operators are polymorphic. On two **sets**: union, intersection, symmetric difference (`{1,2} | {2,3}` → `{1,2,3}`). On two **numbers**: bitwise OR / AND / XOR (`0xF0 & 0x33` → `0x30`). Mixed-type operands raise. Shifts `<<` / `>>` and unary `~` are integer-only. Bitwise math uses Python-style arbitrary-size integers with a safety cap for runaway values, `1 << 61` prints `2305843009213693952`, not a rounded JavaScript number. Augmented forms (`x |= 1`, `x <<= 8`) work on both shapes.
lang_features.bitwise.title: Bitwise & Set Operators
lang_features.classes.description: Bundle data and behavior together. `__init__(self, ...)` sets up each instance (`self.count = 0`), and methods take `self` first. **In a machine script the top-level `self` is the machine; inside a method `self` is the object**, pass the machine in if a method needs to drive it. The editor autocompletes `instance.` members and flows method return types through chains.
lang_features.classes.title: Classes
lang_features.dataclasses.description: Import `dataclass` and `field` from `dataclasses` to turn annotated class attributes into declaration-ordered constructor fields. `dataclass` supports `init`, `repr`, `eq`, `order`, and `kw_only`; `field` supports `default`, `default_factory`, `init`, `repr`, `compare`, and `kw_only`. Mutable or otherwise unhashable direct defaults are rejected; use `default_factory` to create a separate value for each instance. Generated behavior includes inherited fields, `__init__`, `__repr__`, exact-class equality, optional ordering, and `__post_init__`. The compatibility spellings `frozen=False`, `unsafe_hash=False`, `slots=False`, and `weakref_slot=False` are accepted, but their `True` behavior is not supported. `match_args` and `ClassVar` / `InitVar` field semantics are unsupported; canonical uses receive a clear error. `MISSING`, `KW_ONLY`, `Field`, `FrozenInstanceError`, `is_dataclass`, `asdict`, `astuple`, `replace`, `fields`, `make_dataclass`, and public `__dataclass_fields__` introspection are unavailable; annotation types stay erased. A dataclass is still an ordinary user-class instance: use it when a record needs methods, validation, value equality, or ordering. Use `TypedDict` when the value is fundamentally a mapping or must cross a JSON-shaped boundary such as the Signal Bus or notebook APIs.
lang_features.dataclasses.title: @dataclass
lang_features.decorators.description: `@deco` above a `def` or `class` wraps it: `name = deco(name)`. Stack them, and pass arguments (`@deco(arg)`). Built-in method decorators: `@staticmethod` (no `self`), `@classmethod` (receives the class as `cls`), and `@property`. The standard `dataclasses` module provides `@dataclass` for generated record-class behavior.
lang_features.decorators.title: Decorators
lang_features.dicts.title: Dictionaries
lang_features.dunder_methods.description: Define what operators and builtins do on your objects. `__eq__` / `__lt__` power `==` and `<`; `__add__` (and reflected `__radd__`) power `+`; `__len__`, `__bool__`, `__getitem__`, `__contains__`, `__iter__`, `__call__`, and `__str__` / `__repr__` dispatch from `len()`, truthiness, `x[k]`, `in`, `for`, calling, and `print`. Operator overloads must be **pure**, they cannot `sleep()` or change game state.
lang_features.dunder_methods.title: Operators & dunder methods
lang_features.for_loop.description: Iterate over a list, tuple, or range. Supports `break`, `continue`, tuple-unpack targets (`for k, v in d.items():`), and an optional `else:` block that runs when the loop ends without `break`. Loop control belongs to the current function/class-free loop body; a nested helper or class cannot break or continue its caller's loop.
lang_features.for_loop.title: For Loop
lang_features.functions.description: Define reusable blocks of code. Parameters can have default values (`def f(x, n=10): ...`), and callers can use either positional args (`f(5, 20)`) or keyword args (`f(5, n=20)`), same as Python. All positional args must come before any keyword args at the call site. Optional type annotations document intent: `def scan(site: MiningSite) -> Site:`. They help the editor with hover and autocomplete, but they do not change how the script runs.
lang_features.functions.title: Functions
lang_features.generators.description: A `def` that contains `yield` is a generator: calling it returns a lazy iterator that produces one value each time it is asked, instead of building the whole list up front. Loop over it with `for x in gen():`, pull one value with `next(it)` (raises `StopIteration` when spent, or returns a default with `next(it, fallback)`), or materialize it with `list(gen())`. `yield from other()` re-emits every value from another iterable/generator and evaluates to that generator's `return` value. Advanced control: `gen.send(v)` resumes the paused `yield` with `v`, `gen.throw(error)` raises an exception at that yield, and `gen.close()` stops it (running any `finally`). A generator is one-shot: once exhausted it stays empty. Note: a bare generator expression `(x for x in xs)` is now lazy too, so wrap it in `list(...)` if you need a reusable list. Generators live only in the running script and cannot be sent over the Signal Bus or stored in the Data Archive: `list(...)` them first.
lang_features.generators.title: Generators (yield)
lang_features.if_else.description: Make decisions based on conditions. Use `x if condition else y` when you need to choose one value inline.
lang_features.if_else.title: If / Else
lang_features.inheritance.description: `class Dog(Animal):` inherits `Animal`'s methods and attributes. Override any of them, and call the base version with `super().method(...)`. Multiple inheritance resolves by Python's C3 MRO, so cooperative `super()` works across a diamond. `isinstance(x, Animal)` and `issubclass(Dog, Animal)` walk the chain.
lang_features.inheritance.title: Inheritance & super()
lang_features.lists.description: Ordered collections and fixed pairs of values.
lang_features.lists.title: Lists & Tuples
lang_features.match_case.description: Branch on the shape of a value. Supports literal cases, `_` wildcard, variable captures, `|` alternatives, `if` guards, list/tuple patterns with `*rest`, and dict-style patterns. An unguarded capture or `_` always matches and must be the final reachable case; a guard may still fall through. Mapping-pattern keys must be unique (`True` and `1` count as the same key). Dict-style patterns also work with fixed result objects, e.g. `result = self.input.take("iron_ore", 10)` followed by `case {"status": "ok", "moved": moved}:`.
lang_features.match_case.title: Match / Case
lang_features.print.title: Print
lang_features.properties.description: `@property` turns a method into a computed attribute read **without parens** (`tank.level`, not `tank.level()`). Add `@name.setter` so `tank.level = 42` runs validation. Use it to expose derived or guarded state while keeping plain attribute syntax.
lang_features.properties.title: @property
lang_features.raw_strings.description: Prefix a string with `r` to keep backslashes literal instead of treating them as escapes, handy for `re` patterns so you don't have to double every backslash. `r"\d+"` is the three characters backslash, `d`, `+`. Combine with `f` for raw f-strings (`rf"..."`), where `{...}` interpolation still works but backslashes stay literal. A backslash still escapes the closing quote, so a raw string can't end in an odd number of backslashes.
lang_features.raw_strings.title: Raw Strings
lang_features.regex.description: Import the built-in `re` module for pattern matching, captures, replacements, and regex-based splitting. It works without Shared Library research and returns `Match` objects from `search`, `match`, and `fullmatch`. Pair it with raw strings (`r"..."`) so you don't have to double every backslash in a pattern.
lang_features.regex.title: Regular Expressions
lang_features.typeddict.description: Use `TypedDict("Name", {...})` for small record-shaped structures: controller state, route records, cached scan rows, or the simple data objects you might otherwise reach for a class/decorator to model. Annotate a variable with it (`state: Name`) and the editor autocompletes keys, flows each field's type through both `state["key"]` and `state.key`, and flags a typo'd key **before you run**. At runtime, `state.mode` and `state["mode"]` are equivalent for a dict containing the ordinary string key `"mode"`; built-in dict method names still resolve as methods. `TypedDict` adds a stable declared shape so the editor can autocomplete and type-check those fields even when the value flows through other code.
lang_features.typeddict.title: TypedDict (record shapes)
lang_features.variables.description: Store values for later use. No type declarations needed.
lang_features.variables.title: Variables
lang_features.while_loop.description: Repeat code while a condition is true. Supports `break`, `continue`, and an optional `else:` block that runs when the loop ends without `break`. Loop control belongs to the current function/class-free loop body; a nested helper or class cannot break or continue its caller's loop.
lang_features.while_loop.title: While Loop

lightning_rod_script.info:
## Overview

A Lightning Rod catches nearby thunderstorm strikes and banks their energy. It discharges that reserve automatically when its grid runs short and its batteries are empty. Capture and discharge do not require a running script.

## Condition

`self.integrity()` reports condition from **0-1**. Continuous corrosion lowers condition by **0.05 per day**. Strikes do not cause separate damage.

Condition is also capture efficiency. At **0.5**, the rod banks half of the energy it accepts from a strike. At **0**, it still stands and remains repairable, but banks nothing.

## Maintenance

The rod's `self.input` holds Storm Glass supplied through ordinary item logistics. Repairs are not automatic: a running script must call `self.repair()`. One repair consumes **1 Storm Glass** when the rod is worn and restores condition to **1**. At full condition, no Storm Glass is consumed. Without Storm Glass in the input, condition does not change.

Open DOCS for exact method and result contracts.

machines.bio_caster.description: Volcanic automation machine, step 3 of the volcanic loop, between Bio Lab and Bio Exchange. Forges a fragment by holding the crucible in the order's target temperature band (steam heats it up, water cools it down) with the right fabricated materials loaded, then casting. Its 20 t steam and water process buffers each need an explicit `FluidPort.connect(...)` relationship to a compatible source. Local sources transfer directly; remote sources also need a completed conflict-free pipe route between both locations. Idle until scripted: drive the two knobs, verify the band + materials, and cast, a cast out of band or with the wrong materials burns the whole charge.
machines.bio_caster.name: Bio Caster
machines.bio_collector.description: Automation machine for step 1 of the biology loop, programmatically retrieves a specimen from the field. Single cargo slot; mirrors the manual COLLECT button.
machines.bio_collector.name: Bio Collector
machines.bio_conditioner.description: Deep automation machine, step 3 of the deep loop, between Bio Lab and Bio Exchange. Quality-control inspection: reads a fragment's condition report and runs a 5-stage accept/reject gauntlet against a published rulebook; pass all five and it's conditioned for an order. Power-only, idle until scripted, one wrong call burns the specimen.
machines.bio_conditioner.name: Bio Conditioner
machines.bio_exchange.description: Fills authored Bio Orders for credit rewards. Scripts stage exact samples through the input port; surplus in-transit samples return through the output port without losing properties.
machines.bio_exchange.name: Bio Exchange
machines.bio_lab.description: Automation machine for steps 2 and 3. Scripts route reagents through the input port and exact property-bearing samples through the output port. Manual Biology uses the workbench's one stockroom: Base Inventory at Nocturna Base, or an explicitly selected local Warehouse at another outpost.
machines.bio_lab.name: Bio Lab
machines.bio_luminizer.description: Coastal automation machine, step 3 of the coastal loop, between Bio Lab and Bio Exchange. Tunes a bioluminescent fragment's glow to an order's exact target color with three impure tint lamps. Idle until scripted: read the start glow, the target, and the lamp signatures, solve the lamp settings, and infuse.
machines.bio_luminizer.name: Bio Luminizer

machines.charging_station.name: Vehicle Charging Station

machines.clock.name: Clock

machines.gps.name: GPS
machines.grow_lamp.description: Lights the four orthogonally adjacent field cells (directly above, below, left, and right) while powered and enabled.
machines.grow_lamp.name: Grow Lamp

machines.inventory.description: Physical storage room at Nocturna Base. It starts with 36 slots and 10 units per stack. It is not a freight endpoint for remote outposts.

machines.large_warehouse.description: High-bay multi-material depot, 15 material-locked slots, 2,000 each (30,000 total). Broad enough to stage a full biological catalogue.
machines.large_warehouse.name: Large Warehouse
machines.lead_cask.description: Shielded storage for hot cargo. Raw Uranium and Fuel Rods live here and nowhere else on the stationary side. Its 100-unit stock is the buffer between storms and reactor burn.
machines.lead_cask.name: Lead Cask
machines.lightning_rod.description: A 4,000 Wh storm-charged reserve catching strikes within 600 m. Condition falls 0.05 per day, reducing capture to zero unless a running script repairs it with one Storm Glass.
machines.lightning_rod.name: Lightning Rod
machines.liquid_tank.description: Passive buffer that holds any one liquid, water, oil, or a biome essence. It commits to the first liquid piped in.
machines.liquid_tank.name: Liquid Tank
machines.mining_drill.description: Mk I static drill for hardness-1 deposits: 25 t/h at standard purity and 10 W while extracting.
machines.mining_drill.name: Mining Drill

machines.mining_drill_heavy.name: Heavy Mining Drill
machines.mining_drill_industrial.description: Mk II static drill for hardness-3 deposits: 75 t/h at standard purity and 35 W while extracting.
machines.mining_drill_industrial.name: Industrial Mining Drill
machines.nuclear_battery.description: Dense grid-charged storage cell, 15,000 Wh, thirty times a base battery. Joins the battery pool: charges on surplus, carries the night.
machines.nuclear_battery.name: Nuclear Battery
machines.offline: {name} is offline. Power it on first.

machines.oil_generator.name: Oil Generator

machines.oil_pump.name: Oil Pump
machines.outpost_hub.description: An outpost on the planet. Begins with a soft capacity of **20** buildings, expandable to **25** through research. Power lines touching its utility footprint join one power subnet. Fluid components touching that utility footprint remain physically separate and become available to compatible player-connected local machines; the outpost stores no fluid itself. Founded from a Planet Map blueprint, placed in Plan Mode or by script, and physically built by a Constructor-equipped Pioneer.

machines.oxygen_generator.description: Converts atmospheric CO2 into oxygen. Script controls intake rate and waste management; powered draw is 8 W at Mk I and scales with Mk tier.
machines.oxygen_generator.name: Oxygen Generator
machines.oxygen_sensor.description: Atmospheric oxygen level monitor. Requires calibration.
machines.oxygen_sensor.name: Oxygen Sensor
machines.pioneer.description: Eight-slot modular expedition chassis with no built-in battery, cargo, or Nav. The bare chassis cannot move until separately purchased hardware is installed.
machines.pioneer.name: Pioneer
machines.plant_terraformer.accepts: Forage, Salt, Fertilizer, and Growth Accelerant
machines.plant_terraformer.accessible_summary: {status}. The Plants ladder is {progress}% complete, currently {phase}. Loaded Forage: {forage}.
machines.plant_terraformer.description: The sole converter from harvested physical Forage to permanent Plants km². mining_drill_script.info:
## Overview

A static Mining Drill sits on a surveyed mineral site and extracts ore automatically while powered, no move loop, no dig commands. Mk I cuts hardness **1**, Mk II cuts up to **3**, and Mk III cuts up to **4**. Higher tiers also extract faster, while site **purity** multiplies speed. Ore lands in the drill's internal stockpile and extraction stops when it is full.

## What your script does

• **Expose the stockpile.** `self.output.count()`, `capacity()`, and `stacks()` report what is waiting. This pickup-only output has no `connect()` or `send()` method.
• **Send a carrier.** A Rover or Pioneer must physically reach the Drill, connect its own input to the Drill, and call `take(...)`. A drone calls `go_to_drill(name)`, then `cargo.load(...)`, and flies the ore to a Depot.
• **Watch the rate.** `self.drill_rate()` is the live t/h extraction; **0** means unpowered, off-site, incompatible with the deposit hardness, or stockpile full.

> The drill draws no power when it cannot extract. If its stockpile is full, send a carrier and empty it. If the deposit is too hard, deploy the required drill tier.

oil_generator_script.info:
## Overview

The Oil Generator burns oil to produce up to **700 W** from a single machine, several times a Steam Turbine's peak. `throttle` is **0-1**; with enough oil supplied, power output and oil demand scale linearly. At full throttle it demands **8 t/h** and consumes that rate while fully supplied. A buffered pure well always sustains one full generator and produces enough for almost two on average. A typical rich well also sustains one, while its shortest-duty cycles need slightly lower generator throttle or a second source. Oil remains shared with refinery products and heli-drone fuel, so storage and load control still matter.

Default `throttle = 0`. The generator idles until a script sets a value.

## What your script does

The generator's role is **buffered bridge and load-following power**:

• Day with strong solar → throttle to **0** (oil is expensive).
• Solar dim or absent (night, dust) → throttle up to cover deficit.
• Critical demand spike (Mk III machines kicking in) → throttle high briefly.
• Oil tank near empty → throttle down to preserve the buffer until pumps catch up.

Read a base battery as a grid-load proxy (`get_component("battery_1").get_level() / get_component("battery_1").get_capacity()`, low = grid is starving, throttle up; high = grid has surplus, throttle down) and the oil tank's `fill_pct()` to drive the decision. The generator publishes `self.power_output()` and `self.oil_consumption()` so your script can verify it's actually contributing.

## Common pitfall

> If the `oil_in` buffer empties mid-burn, actual output and `oil_consumption()` both drop with the oil available during that tick. A generator at `throttle = 1.0` with a starved input produces less than one at `throttle = 0.6` with a full input. Watch `power_output()` and `oil_consumption()` rather than `throttle()` when judging real grid contribution.

oil_pump_script.info:
## Overview

An Oil Pump is bolted onto a surveyed oil well. Peak flow rate is `8 / 16 / 24 t/h` for `standard` / `rich` / `pure` yields, multiplied by the pump's `throttle` (**0-1**). Power draw also scales with throttle, and the pump idles at `throttle = 0` by default.

Oil wells **pulse**: each well runs its own rhythm of active and dormant phases, several hours each. A dormant well delivers nothing at any throttle, `self.well_active()` reads the current phase, and a Liquid Tank downstream carries the chain through the gaps.

## What your script does

Pumps fill the chain that feeds the Oil Generator (`~8 t/h` at full output) and oil-product recipes in the Fabricator (lubricant, plastic, rubber, tar). A buffered pure well always sustains one full generator and produces enough for almost two on average. A typical rich well also sustains one, but a short-active, long-dormant rich well needs slightly lower generator throttle or a second source. A typical script keeps the pump at **1.0** unless the downstream Liquid Tank fills past a threshold, at which point it throttles back to avoid wasted draw.

• Watch the Liquid Tank's `fill_pct()` from a remote read, throttle to **0.3** above **0.9**.
• Coordinate with the Oil Generator's `throttle()`, if the generator is idle, the pump's only job is keeping the tank topped up.

## Common pitfall

> Oil flows through liquid pipes (`liquid_pipe_segment`), not gas pipes. Laying a gas-pipe-only network from the pump means no flow reaches the tank and `pump_rate()` will read **0** even when the pump is active and the well has yield. Verify the pipe medium matches the fluid.

oxygen_gen.info:
## Overview

The generator converts atmospheric CO₂ into oxygen through electrolysis. Carbon waste is stored inside the machine.

## Intake

The reaction chamber reaches peak efficiency when intake is set to **CO₂ / 10** for the current atmospheric CO₂ level. Values above or below that point reduce efficiency smoothly.

## Waste

Carbon waste builds up during operation. The machine runs at full efficiency up to **60 waste**. Above **60**, efficiency drops steadily. At **100**, the machine stalls completely.

The waste exhaust port operates most cleanly when waste is in the **50-60** range. Clearing outside that range strains the mechanism, the further from the safe range, the more conversion efficiency is lost until the next clearance. Scripts read the active penalty with `self.dump_penalty()`.

## What your script does

In pseudocode: *loop forever, read the CO₂ level, set intake to `CO₂ / 10`, dump waste when it lands in the 50-60 sweet spot.*

Read atmospheric conditions with `get_component("atmosphere")`.

panel.bar_chart:
Multi-bar comparison chart, themed alternating colors, optional labels under each bar. `max` is optional, omit to auto-scale to the largest value.

```preview
bar_chart(0, 0, 0, 0, [42, 80, 26, 61, 95], 100)
```
panel.button:
A clickable button. Pass a unique `key` so the click routes back to it. Returns `True` the single tick it's pressed (momentary), branch on it: `if panel.button("shed", 10, 12): power.set_powered(...)`. `w`/`h` default to **90×26**. The first input widget that lets a card *act* on the player's click, not just paint.

```preview
button(10, 12, 90, 26, "shed now")
```
panel.card:
Bordered subsection with optional title bar. Use to group related content visually, mirrors the dashboard's card aesthetic.

```preview
card(8, 8, 264, 64, "Section")
```
panel.clear: Wipe the panel canvas. Call at the top of every `while True:` loop iteration so old paint doesn't ghost behind new paint.
panel.counter:
Big-number stat block, large value on top, small uppercase label below. Use for headline numbers (credits, day count, ingot inventory). `size` defaults to **24**.

```preview
counter(16, 38, 87, "shipped", 26)
```
panel.divider:
Horizontal or vertical separator line in the muted border color. Use to break a panel into visual zones.

```preview
divider(10, 40, 270, 40)
```
panel.draw_circle:
Outlined circle in the given color.

```preview
draw_circle(140, 40, 24, "accent")
```
panel.draw_icon:
Render any icon from the game's item catalog at the requested size (default **32** pixels). Item id is the same string you'd pass to `inventory` / `storage_bin` APIs (`"iron_ore"`, `"iron_ingot"`, `"water"`, etc.), plus things you never hold such as fluids and creatures. `panel.icon_ids()` returns the full list, and every item's own page lives under **Database** in this panel. Unknown ids no-op silently.

```preview
draw_icon()
```
panel.draw_rect:
Outlined rectangle in the given color (defaults to `"border"`). Use for custom subsection borders or visual frames.

```preview
draw_rect(10, 10, 260, 60, "accent")
```
panel.draw_text:
Text rendered in monospace at the given size. Optional `wrap` (pixel width) enables greedy word-wrapping into a multi-line block, useful for log feeds and order briefings. Color accepts theme tokens or hex.

```preview
draw_text(10, 24, "Hello, panel.", 14, "text-bright")
```
panel.fill_circle:
Filled disc in the given color.

```preview
fill_circle(140, 40, 24, "warning")
```
panel.fill_rect:
Filled rectangle in the given color (defaults to `"accent"`). Use for backgrounds, progress fills, color blocks.

```preview
fill_rect(10, 10, 260, 60, "success")
```
panel.gauge:
Three-quarter-circle dial with arc fill. `fraction` clamps to **0-1**, sweeping **270°** from bottom-left around to bottom-right. Optional center label sits in the middle (typically the value as text).

```preview
gauge(140, 50, 32, 0.62, "62%")
```
panel.height: Current logical canvas height in pixels: **200** for a one-row card or **400** for a two-row card. Use for ratio-based positioning.
panel.icon_ids:
List of every id `draw_icon` can render, sorted. Covers more than the items you can hold: fluids, creatures, essences, and machine art all have icons. Use it to build a picker, validate an id before drawing, or just print the catalog once while you are writing a card.

```
for icon in panel.icon_ids():
  print(icon)
```
panel.label:
Semantically styled text. `style` accepts `"title"` (bright, bold), `"caption"` (muted, uppercase), `"muted"` (secondary), `"value"` (numeric readout). Defaults to `"title"`. Use instead of `draw_text` when you want the dashboard's text hierarchy applied automatically.

```preview
label(10, 30, "OXYGEN", "caption")
```
panel.pill:
Rounded badge with text, achievement-style. Color accepts theme tokens (`"accent"`, `"success"`, `"warning"`, `"error"`, `"text-muted"`) or hex. Use for status labels or category tags.

```preview
pill(10, 22, "earned", "success")
```
panel.progress_bar:
Horizontal fill bar with track + filled accent. `fraction` clamps to **0-1**. Color defaults to `"accent"`; use `"success"`, `"warning"`, `"error"` for traffic-light cues.

```preview
progress_bar(0.72, "success")
```
panel.slider:
A horizontal slider the player clicks to set a value. Pass a unique `key`; `default` (**0-1**) sets the starting value. Returns the current value as a **0-1** number every tick, persisted in the card's state. Use it for thresholds the player tunes live, a buy-trigger level, a throttle target.

```preview
slider(10, 14, 120, 0.5, "rate")
```
panel.spark_line:
Compact trend line drawn from a numeric series. Player accumulates values into a list and pushes the most recent on each tick, the widget normalizes to the series' min/max range and fills a subtle area below the line. Empty / single-value series no-op.

```preview
spark_line(0, 0, 0, 0)
```
panel.status_dot:
Colored disc resolved from a status string. Recognized values: `"running"` (green), `"paused"` (warning), `"error"` (error red), `"idle"` (muted). Renders with a subtle outer glow ring. Useful for per-row indicators in machine lists.

```preview
status_dot(0, 0, 5, "running")
```
panel.switch:
An interactive on/off switch, the player clicks it to flip. Pass a unique `key`; `default_on` sets the starting state the first time the card runs. Returns the current boolean every tick, and the flip persists in the card's state across reloads. Unlike the display `toggle` (which only shows a state you pass in), this one is clickable: `auto = panel.switch("auto_recover", 165, 128, True)`.

```preview
switch(10, 12, true, "auto-recover")
```
panel.toggle:
Green/grey power-toggle pill matching the dashboard's machine on/off control. This widget only displays the `on` value you pass in; use `panel.switch(...)` for a clickable control.

```preview
toggle(10, 12, true, "powered")
```
panel.vertical_bar:
Vertical fill bar, fills from the bottom up. Same `fraction` and color rules as `progress_bar`. Use when the panel layout favors verticality (multi-tank stacks, atmospheric stacks).

```preview
vertical_bar(110, 10, 30, 60, 0.6)
```
panel.width: Current logical canvas width in pixels: **500** for a one-column card or **1000** for a two-column card. Use for ratio-based positioning.

pioneer_script.info:
## Overview

A modular expedition vehicle for longer and heavier ground trips than the Rover. Its eight Universal slots accept Nav, Sonar, Drill, Constructor, Battery Holder, and Cargo Rack modules. Sport Nav modules can stack; the other function capabilities are limited to one each.

## Batteries and range

Battery Holders carry Portable Batteries, and every installed battery contributes to one pool exposed through `self.battery`. No installed battery means no movement. Sport Nav modules increase speed and power draw, while loaded cargo adds movement cost, so long routes reward deliberate battery, cargo, and throttle choices.

## Cargo

Cargo Racks carry Portable Storage Bins. All installed bins form one logical `self.cargo` surface, while `self.cargo.racks()` exposes the physical layout. Each bin latches to one item id until it is emptied.

After Auto Feeders, `self.input` and `self.output` transfer cargo to Inventory only inside the home outpost's service area, or to Storage Bins, Warehouses, outpost machines, and nearby stopped cargo vehicles at the Pioneer's current location. Inventory is not present at remote outposts. Vehicle handoffs require both vehicles to be stopped within about 2 m.

## Finding sites: don't roam

Every "?" contact sits on the map from the start. Don't send the Pioneer wandering: `get_component("nocturna").points_of_interest()` lists every contact with `.x`, `.y`, and `.scanned`. Filter `if not p.scanned:`, drive to each contact, brake, and sweep with `self.sonar.scan()` + `survey()`. A contact's `.kind` reads `"unknown"` until you scan it: you know where the sites are, not what they are.

## Construction and movement

A mounted Constructor exposes `self.constructor` for executing planned blueprints. Nav commands are script-owned: keep the route script active until it is close enough, then brake before construction or another stationary action. Stopping the script, reaching its end, or hitting an uncaught error also stops the Pioneer and clears its active route.

## Modifying the rig

At an outpost service area, use `self.modules()`, `self.mount(...)`, `self.unmount(...)`, `self.install(...)`, and `self.uninstall(...)` to evolve the rig as better hardware unlocks.

Biological scanning and extraction are drone-only capabilities. Pioneer slots do not accept Portable Bio modules.

plant_terraformer_script.info:
## Overview

The Plant Terraformer is the only machine that creates permanent Plants km². It consumes harvested Forage and the support materials required by the current phase.

## Item input

Use the standard `self.input.connect(source)` and `self.input.take(item_id, amount)` API after Auto Feeders research. The source may be home Inventory, a local Storage Bin or Warehouse, or a local machine output such as a Crop Automator. The input has one connection at a time; reconnect it when you need to load a different source. Sources can also call their normal `output.send(...)` method.

Transfers obey the ordinary cooldown and endpoint-lock rules. The Terraformer's destination feeder moves **16 items per handling step** at Mk I and **80** at Mk II, whether the source pushes or the Terraformer pulls. Fast Feeders research halves the duration of all timed item transfers, including these. Direct Crop Automator to Terraformer transfers avoid the extra Warehouse leg.

Water uses `self.water_in`. Connect it to a compatible water source. A remote source also needs a completed conflict-free Liquid Pipe route between both locations. The input holds one full Forage batch, the Salt that batch needs, and up to **10 of each** Fertilizer tier and Growth Accelerant.

## Batches

When a cycle can start, the machine commits the largest whole Forage batch every loaded material can support. If there are 10 Forage but Water for 8, it loads 8. If any required material cannot support one Forage, it waits. `self.batch_requirements()` reports the full next recipe, while `self.batch_size()` reports what can load now.

Salt is consumed as whole items at cycle start: **1 per 500 Forage**, rounded up for each batch. A full Mk I batch consumes **3 Salt** and a full Mk II batch consumes **14 Salt**. Unused treatment value does not carry over. `self.input.count("salt")` reports every remaining Salt item.

Fertilizer Mk I, Mk II, and Mk III contribute **10**, **30**, and **50 potency**. Any whole-item combination may reach the rounded target. Each cycle spends stored potency first, consuming additional whole items only to cover the shortfall. Unused potency stays in the machine for later batches and survives save/load. One Mk III item supplies 50 potency; a 27-potency batch leaves 23. The card shows total available potency, including both stored potency and unopened items. Its tier badges and `self.input.count(item_id)` count only unopened items. Growth Accelerant is a whole-item count with no potency. A full Mk II batch asks for **27 Fertilizer potency** and, in the final phase, **1 Growth Accelerant**.

Items and Water are consumed when the cycle starts. The cycle then runs for **3 hours** at 100% outpost efficiency and delivers its km². When it finishes, the next affordable loaded batch starts immediately. Power loss or disabling pauses the in-flight batch without losing it.

A Mk I batch holds up to **1,200 Forage** and stops with `"needs_mk2"` at 2,250,000 km². A Mk II batch holds up to **6,600 Forage** and supports Fertilizer and Growth Accelerant.
plant_terraformer_script.template:
self.input.connect("crop_automator_1")
self.set_enabled(True)

while True:
  if self.input.count("forage") < self.batch_requirements()["forage"]:
    self.input.take("forage", self.batch_requirements()["forage"])
  print(self.status(), self.batch_size())
  sleep(1)

pressure_gen.info:
## Overview

The pressure generator compresses atmospheric gas in a resonance chamber. Its gauge sweeps across **0-100** over and over. Each sweep has a small sync window. Call `self.sync()` while `self.gauge()` is between `self.next_window_low()` and `self.next_window_high()`.

A hit adds **+25%** efficiency. A miss, or no sync before the gauge wraps, subtracts **10%**. Efficiency is floored at **0%**.

## What your script does

Read the window and gauge in the same loop. The window values are for the sweep happening now. They change when the gauge wraps into the next sweep, so do not read them once at startup and reuse them forever.

In pseudocode: *loop forever, read the current sync window, read the gauge, and sync when the gauge is inside that window.*

Only the first `sync()` attempt in a sweep counts. Extra calls before the gauge wraps do nothing.

## Common pitfall

The `next_` in `next_window_low()` refers to the sync opportunity in the sweep currently underway.

Efficiency takes several good sweeps to settle. Four consecutive hits bring it to **100%**, and a miss costs **10%**.

> A fresh start reads **0%** efficiency and **0** pressure until your first sync lands, then climbs in **+25%** steps. Seeing 0% for the first few sweeps is the resonance settling, not a fault.

reactor_script.info:
## Overview

The Reactor turns Fuel Rods and cooling water into up to **5,000 W**. `set_heat(value)` accepts a value from **0** to **1**, and temperature changes gradually in response.

The reactor's internal condition changes every **12 hours**. The condition is not reported, so the same heat setting can lead to a different temperature after a change.

## Temperature bands

• Below **300 °C**: no output.
• **300-600 °C**, yellow: output rises from **0%** to **50%**.
• **600-900 °C**, green: output rises from **50%** to **100%**. Peak output is exactly **900 °C**.
• **900-950 °C**, red: output falls back from **100%** to **0%** as the core keeps climbing.
• At **950 °C**: the reactor overheats, shuts down, and cools automatically. It returns to service after reaching **600 °C**.

## Supplies

While heating, the cooling loop automatically consumes **0.5-1 t/h** from `water_in`, based on the heat setting. If the loop runs dry, heating and fuel use pause until water returns.

The active Fuel Rod is consumed gradually based on the heat setting. When it runs out, the reactor automatically takes the next Fuel Rod from `input`. `input` is a normal input slot with `connect()`, `take()`, `flush()`, `count()`, `capacity()`, and `connected_to()`.

## Readouts

`heat()` reports the current heat setting. `temperature()`, `power_output()`, and `fuel_level()` report the current machine values. The possible `status()` values are `"running"`, `"overheated"`, `"no_fuel"`, and `"no_coolant"`.

## Writing the controller

Temperature settles at `heat` multiplied by a hidden gain, so the gain is not readable but it is measurable: once temperature stops moving, it equals `temperature()` divided by `heat()`. Dividing your target by that gain gives the heat that holds it, which is why a controller that measures beats one built on a fixed constant.

> Correction strength is applied once per loop, but the core moves per **world-clock hour**, and one world-clock hour is a fixed number of real seconds that the game speed can change. A loop tuned at one speed will over- or under-correct at another unless it scales by `clock.real_seconds_per_hour()`.

refiner_script.info:
## Overview

The Refiner converts RAW exotic fluids from uncommon and rare deposits into their usable forms. It is a mixed-input recipe machine: exotic feedstock flows in through `gas_in` / `liquid_in`, tar enters through `self.input`, and refined product flows out through `gas_out` / `liquid_out`.

## What your script does

• **Pick the refinement.** `self.list_recipes()` → `self.set_recipe(recipe_id)`; recipes unlock via Bio Orders. A Recipe's `.input_fluid` is the exact raw fluid, `.fluid_inputs` gives input-port tons per run, `.inputs` gives the tar cost, and `.output_fluid` / `.fluid_outputs` identify the refined product and output port.
• **Wire both fluid sides.** Connect the input port named in `.fluid_inputs` to the matching raw-fluid source, then connect the port named in `.fluid_outputs` to storage. Remote relationships also need completed conflict-free matching pipe routes; a full output stalls the run.
• **Load tar.** Connect `self.input` to a local tar store and pull the recipe's required amount. No tar means no refining.
• **Monitor.** `self.is_running()`, `self.is_stalled()`, `self.get_rate()`, `self.get_progress()`.

> Rarer refinements consume more tar and draw noticeably more power, check both the reagent supply and grid headroom before switching to a heavier recipe.

research.eta_tooltip: Estimated time to this track's next unlock at the current production rate, shown in game time, not real time. Reads "stalled" when nothing is producing toward it, "ready" when the meter has already passed the gate, and a dash only when no estimate can be made at all.
research.title: RESEARCH

researches.advanced_biopolymers.description: Unlocks the Fabricator recipe for **Reinforced Biopolymer**. The composite joins established oil, plant, and water production into a structural material used by large Earth orders and advanced biological chemistry.
researches.advanced_biopolymers.name: Advanced Biopolymers
researches.auto_feeders.description: Unlocks property-preserving item flow through machine I/O ports. Inventory is a source or destination only at Nocturna Base; other endpoints must be at the machine's outpost or physically present vehicle location. Equal item ids with different properties remain distinct stacks.
researches.auto_feeders.name: Auto Feeders
researches.battery_holder_large.description: Unlocks the Large Battery Holder in the shop. Three bays, enough capacity to sustain Heavy Drill power draw on long edge-ring expeditions.
researches.battery_holder_large.name: Large Battery Holder
researches.battery_holder_medium.description: Unlocks the Medium Battery Holder in the shop. Two bays for portable batteries, a compact range upgrade for modular vehicles.
researches.battery_holder_medium.name: Medium Battery Holder
researches.battery_holder_small.description: Unlocks the Small Battery Holder in the shop. Adds a **1**-bay portable battery mount for modular vehicles, essential for any expedition away from the Vehicle Charging Station.
researches.battery_holder_small.name: Battery Holder
researches.bio_caster.description: Unlocks the Bio Caster in the shop, the volcanic machine that heat-casts a fragment with fabricated materials. Volcanic Bio Orders require forged fragments.
researches.bio_caster.name: Volcanic Forge-Casting
researches.bio_conditioner.description: Unlocks the Bio Conditioner in the shop, the deep machine that quality-control-inspects a fragment through a 5-stage accept/reject gauntlet against a published rulebook. Deep Bio Orders require conditioned fragments. Power-only, no fluids or materials.
researches.bio_conditioner.name: Deep-Sea Conditioning
researches.biomass_mixer_mk2_pack.description: Unlocks the Biomass Mixer Mk II Upgrade Pack in the shop. One pack retrofits one deployed Mk I Mixer for **4.5× output** on only **2.4× essence consumption**, with **5× power draw**. That is **87.5%** more biomass per ton of essence, which matters because Liquifier intake is fixed and rare life forms regrow slowly. There is no Mk III.
researches.biomass_mixer_mk2_pack.name: Biomass Mixer Mk II
researches.biomass_mixer_mk2_pack.short: 87.5% more biomass per ton of essence.
researches.biosphere.description: Unlocks the **Biomass tier** supply chain and makes the Portable Bio Scanner, Portable Bio Extractor, Essence Liquifier, and Biomass Mixer available in the Shop. Scan biome tiles, extract life-form samples, and run them through the chain to produce biomass.
researches.biosphere.name: Biosphere
researches.camera_feed.description: Bring the exterior camera online and watch the world outside through a live feed. Storms cross the basin, ice gives way, strange life takes hold, and the base you built glows against the dark.
researches.camera_feed.name: Camera Feed
researches.camera_feed.short: Watch Nocturna change in real time.
researches.cargo_expansion.description: Unlocks the **EXPAND** button on the Inventory page. Each slot costs more than the last, starting at **500 cr** for slot 37 and climbing to ~**146,000 cr** for the final slot, capped at **60** total. Total cost to fully max out: ~**666,000 cr**.
researches.cargo_expansion.name: Cargo Expansion
researches.cargo_rack_large.description: Unlocks the Large Cargo Rack in the shop. Three bins for maximum haul capacity on large mining runs.
researches.cargo_rack_large.name: Large Cargo Rack
researches.cargo_rack_medium.description: Unlocks the Medium Cargo Rack and Heavy Portable Bin in the shop. Two bins for larger hauls per run, with room for a second mineral.
researches.cargo_rack_medium.name: Medium Cargo Rack
researches.cargo_rack_small.description: Unlocks the Small Cargo Rack and Portable Bin in the shop. A **1**-bin rack for modular vehicles, letting them haul mined ore back to base.
researches.cargo_rack_small.name: Cargo Rack
researches.cartography.description: Adds map markers: named, colored annotations you place in Plan Mode or from any script with `get_component("markers")`. Markers are notes, not construction. They cost nothing, need no Pioneer, and appear the moment you place them, so a survey script can record what it found where it found it.
researches.cartography.name: Cartography
researches.charging_station.description: Unlocks the Vehicle Charging Station in the Shop. Mk I has **1 bay** and a **30 W** charging budget; later packs raise both fleet capacity and pooled solo charging speed.
researches.charging_station.name: Vehicle Charging Station
researches.charging_station_mk2_pack.description: Unlocks the Vehicle Charging Station Mk II Upgrade Pack in the shop. Retrofits a deployed station to Mk II, adding a second charging bay.
researches.charging_station_mk2_pack.name: Vehicle Charging Station Mk II
researches.charging_station_mk2_pack.short: Second bay; pools to 120 W solo.
researches.constructor_module.description: Unlocks the Constructor Module for the Pioneer in the Shop. Plan construction in Planet Map Plan Mode or with `get_component("construction_blueprint")`, load the needed kits, segments, or bridges into the Pioneer's cargo, and drive out to build outposts, pipes, power lines, and machines on site.
researches.constructor_module.name: Constructor Module
researches.custom_panels.description: Opens the Control Room, a top-level page for script-driven dashboard cards. Build clocks, fleet boards, vent-cycle timelines, and recovery controls with drawing and input APIs.
researches.custom_panels.name: Control Room
researches.data_archive.description: Adds the Data Archive tab to the Ship Computer. Scripts can store lookup tables, calibration samples, discovered maps, and other learned knowledge that persists across restarts and save/load. Use the Signal Bus for live coordination and the Data Archive for long-lived data.
researches.data_archive.name: Data Archive
researches.deep_exotics.description: Unlocks sonar discovery, extraction, and refining for the **rarest** exotic gases and liquids used by late-stage Habitat requirements.
researches.deep_exotics.name: Deep Exotics
researches.deep_extraction.description: Unlocks Drill modules in the shop. Extract raw ore from surveyed mining sites.
researches.deep_extraction.name: Drill Module
researches.dispatch_mk2.description: Quadruples each Supply Dock's per-pulse emission count from **1** to **4** units, so the effective rate jumps from **25 units/h** to **100 units/h**. Pulse cadence is unchanged; only the packet size scales.
researches.dispatch_mk2.name: Bulk Logistics II
researches.dispatch_mk3.description: Bumps each Supply Dock's per-pulse emission to **16** units, an effective **400 units/h**. Pulse cadence is unchanged; only the packet size scales.
researches.dispatch_mk3.name: Bulk Logistics III
researches.dispenser.description: Unlocks the **Dispenser Kit recipe**. Fabricate the kit at a Fabricator, then deploy it in a Harvester field to salt the four orthogonally adjacent cells (directly above, below, left, and right) while supplied. Salt is a Water Pump byproduct.
researches.dispenser.name: Dispenser
researches.dna_sequencer.description: Unlocks the DNA Sequencer in the shop, the geothermal machine that reads and rewrites fragment DNA. Geothermal Bio Orders require fragments engineered to carry specific genes.
researches.dna_sequencer.name: Gene Sequencing
researches.drill_heavy.description: Unlocks the Heavy Drill module in the shop. The only drill that can extract hardness-4 Neutronium, required for Mk III fabrication.
researches.drill_heavy.name: Heavy Drill
researches.drill_industrial.description: Unlocks the Industrial Drill module in the shop. Extracts hardness-3 minerals (Rare Earth) from the outer ring. Faster dig time than the basic drill, higher power draw.
researches.drill_industrial.name: Industrial Drill
researches.drones.description: Unlocks the drone system and its fleet dashboard, the Vehicles / Drones / Support roster under the Planet Map. Electric drones fly up to **300 m/h** and consume **5 Wh/h** at full throttle; burn rises with throttle squared. Drone hardware still requires blueprint recipes earned through Earth Orders. Fabricated facilities and chassis deploy from Inventory into outposts; field Mining Drills use Planet Map blueprints placed in Plan Mode or by script.
researches.drones.name: Basic Drone Operations
researches.drones.short: Open aerial logistics before the biosphere era.
researches.earth_clearance.description: Unlocks three advanced contracts as atmospheric oxygen begins to rise.
researches.earth_clearance.name: Earth Clearance
researches.exotic_husbandry.description: Unlocks exotic deposit survey, the **Exotic Gas Cap Kit** and **Exotic Spring Tap Kit** recipes, and the **Refiner** in the Shop. Common and uncommon exotic deposits can now appear on sonar; rare deposits wait for **Deep Exotics**. Capture raw exotic gas or liquid, then refine it into the fluid a Habitat band requires. Fabricate the caps and taps at a Fabricator.
researches.exotic_husbandry.name: Exotic Husbandry
researches.fabricator.description: Unlocks the Fabricator in the Shop. This industrial assembly press combines refined materials into finished equipment, modules, and vehicle frames.
researches.fabricator.name: Fabrication
researches.fast_feeders.description: Reduces the duration of every timed discrete-item transfer by **50%**. Machine endpoints remain occupied until the faster handling cycle finishes. Fluids and manual world actions are unaffected.
researches.fast_feeders.name: Fast Feeders
researches.field_automation.description: Unlocks the **Crop Automator Kit** in the Shop. One automator can queue harvest, plant, and treatment jobs across up to 24 other cells in a centered 5 by 5 area. It executes one at a time in FIFO order by default (first in, first out, so the oldest job runs first), while its script can reorder unfinished work.
researches.field_automation.name: Field Automation
researches.fuel_assembler.description: Unlocks the Fuel Assembler in the Shop. This nuclear workbench presses Raw Uranium and lead casing into **Fuel Rods** and draws about **1,800 W** while running.
researches.fuel_assembler.name: Fuel Assembler
researches.garbage_disposal.description: Unlocks the **Waste Processor Kit recipe**. The machine permanently destroys one selected stream: any item through its feeder input, any liquid through `liquid_in`, or any gas through `gas_in`. This provides an explicit overflow path for tar, surplus water, and unwanted gases without recovering power or materials. Fabricate the kit at a Fabricator; its script selects and enables the active mode.
researches.garbage_disposal.name: Waste Processing
researches.garbage_disposal.short: Programmable destruction for unwanted items and fluids.
researches.geological_survey.description: Extends the Sonar Module to detect thermal vents alongside mining sites. Surveyed vents are added to the Journal with their own readings, so you can find where steam can be tapped.
researches.geological_survey.name: Geological Survey
researches.grow_lamp.description: Unlocks the **Grow Lamp Kit recipe**. Fabricate the kit at a Fabricator, then deploy it in a Harvester field to light the four orthogonally adjacent cells (directly above, below, left, and right). Upgrade packs improve the crops it supports.
researches.grow_lamp.name: Grow Lamp
researches.habitat_development.description: Unlocks the Fabricator recipe for **Enrichment Compound** at **2,000 Wildlife**. This advanced biological material is used in late Earth exports; Habitat adaptations are purchased with Insight and do not consume it.
researches.habitat_development.name: Enrichment Chemistry
researches.habitat_pack_mk2.description: Unlocks the **Habitat Mk II Upgrade Pack recipe** at the Fabricator at **600,000 Wildlife**, after Deep Exotics. Each pack upgrades one Habitat from Mk I to Mk II, doubling its carrying capacity while increasing mature draw to **144-168 W**. Mk II affects capacity only; Insight adaptations control breeding pace and biological costs.
researches.habitat_pack_mk2.name: Habitat Engineering Mk II
researches.heat_mk2_pack.description: Unlocks the Heat Generator Mk II Upgrade Pack in the shop. Retrofits a Mk I heater to Mk II for higher output.
researches.heat_mk2_pack.name: Heat Generator Mk II
researches.heat_mk4_pack.description: Unlocks the **Heat Upgrade Pack Mk IV recipe** at the Fabricator. This final tier **replaces the steam input entirely** with a **Fuel Rod** magazine fed from a connected Lead Cask and draws roughly 100x Mk I power. **A heater with no rod stops producing** rather than degrading.
researches.heat_mk4_pack.name: Heat Generator Mk IV
researches.heat_mk4_pack.short: Nuclear-era heat tier, fuelled by rods.
researches.heavy_portable_battery.description: Unlocks the Heavy Portable Battery in the shop. A **100 Wh** portable cell, double a standard battery, that drops into any vehicle holder bay to sustain long-haul fleets far from the Vehicle Charging Station.
researches.heavy_portable_battery.name: Heavy Portable Battery
researches.heli_drones.description: Allows Heli Thrusters and Oil Tanks to be mounted on drones. Their Fabricator recipes are earned separately through Vestibule orders. Heli drones fly **900 m/h** and consume **5 t/h Oil** at full throttle; burn rises with throttle squared. Three oil-tank sizes set their range, and Drone Service Stations refuel them from their oil input.
researches.heli_drones.name: Heli-Drones
researches.high_bay_warehousing.description: Unlocks the **Large Warehouse** in the shop. It holds **30,000 units** across **15** slots of **2,000**, and each slot sticks to one material. That is enough room for a wide biological and industrial supply chain to keep every material apart, without replacing Drone Depot handoffs or scripted transfers.
researches.high_bay_warehousing.name: Large Warehouse
researches.high_bay_warehousing.short: Fifteen kinds of material in one building.
researches.high_density_storage.description: Rebuilds the shelving at Nocturna Base so each slot takes a taller stack. Items that stack now go up to **20 per slot** instead of **10**. Equipment, modules, and other one-off items still take a slot each. This changes Base Inventory only, not vehicle cargo, Storage Bins, or Warehouses.
researches.high_density_storage.name: Bigger Stacks
researches.high_density_storage.short: Every inventory slot holds twice as much.
researches.high_pressure_fluid_transport.descriptio: Retrofits every completed and future Gas Pipe and Liquid Pipe component. Each matched source-side and sink-side attachment link carries up to **6,000 t/h** instead of **2,000 t/h**. Pipe length and interior branches still add no capacity; separate attachment links and independent components retain their own budgets.
researches.high_pressure_fluid_transport.name: High-Pressure Fluid Transport
researches.high_pressure_fluid_transport.short: Triple remote gas and liquid throughput.
researches.hydrology_survey.description: Unlocks survey of subsurface water deposits and the **Water Pump recipe**. Sonar scans now reveal water wells across the map. Wells produce continuous water at their yield tier (1× / 2× / 3×). Fabricate a Water Pump at a Fabricator, deploy it on a surveyed well, and pipe the output to base.
researches.hydrology_survey.name: Hydrology Survey
researches.large_battery.description: Unlocks the Large Battery in the Shop: **2,500 Wh** of base-station storage, five times the base cell. One unit replaces a cluster of Small Batteries.
researches.large_battery.name: Large Battery
researches.lightning_rod.description: Unlocks the **Lightning Rod Kit recipe**. This storm-charged bank stores **4,000 Wh**, catches strikes within **600 m**, and feeds the grid behind batteries. Condition falls **0.05 per day**, reducing capture to zero unless a script repairs it with **1 Storm Glass**.
researches.lightning_rod.name: Lightning Rods
researches.liquid_tank.description: Unlocks the Liquid Tank in the Shop, a passive **100**-ton buffer that latches to the first liquid it receives (water, oil, or any biome essence) and holds only that fluid until drained.
researches.liquid_tank.name: Liquid Tank
researches.luminizer.description: Unlocks the Bio Luminizer in the shop, the coastal machine that tunes a bioluminescent fragment's glow to an order's exact target color. Coastal Bio Orders require infused fragments.
researches.luminizer.name: Bioluminescent Infusion
researches.mining.description: Unlocks the Mining dashboard, Mining shop category, and planet map. Prospect the surface before committing to a vehicle.
researches.mining.name: Mining Operations
researches.nav_module.description: Unlocks Nav modules in the shop. Gives vehicles the ability to navigate and drive from their own script. Stop, completion, or error cancels script-owned movement.
researches.nav_module.name: Nav Module
researches.nav_sport.description: Unlocks the Sport Nav module in the shop. One Sport Nav gives 2× top speed with 2.6× movement power draw compared with Basic Nav in the same rig, about 1.3× battery use per meter at full throttle. Further Sport Navs stack at a rising cost, especially on loaded long-haul routes.
researches.nav_sport.name: Sport Nav
researches.nuclear_program.description: Unlocks the **Reactor** in the Shop: Fuel Rods in, cooling water through, **5,000 W** out, day and night, storm or calm. One rod lasts **72 hours** at heat **1.0**, and fuel use follows commanded heat. Keep the core in the green band; push it too hot and it overheats and shuts down safely.
researches.nuclear_program.name: Nuclear Program
researches.oil_generator.description: Unlocks the Oil Generator in the shop. Burns oil to produce up to **700 W** from one machine (several times a Steam Turbine's peak) with full throttle control via script. Consumes **8 t/h** at full output.
researches.oil_generator.name: Oil Generator
researches.orders_system.description: A long-range logistics protocol for Earth demand. Supply Docks become available in the Shop and ship **25 units/h** before throughput research; build more docks to serve orders in parallel.
researches.orders_system.name: Supply Logistics
researches.orders_system.short_desc: Unlocks Orders and Supply Dock purchasing.
researches.outpost_expansion.description: Raises the soft building capacity of every current and future outpost by **5**. Nocturna Base increases from **25** to **30** buildings, and founded outposts increase from **20** to **25**. Buildings beyond the new cap still incur the normal overcrowding penalty.
researches.outpost_expansion.name: Outpost Expansion
researches.outpost_expansion.short: Increase every outpost's building capacity by 5.
researches.outpost_hub.description: Unlocks the Outpost Kit in the shop. Founding still requires Constructor Module research plus a Constructor-equipped Pioneer: place an Outpost blueprint in Plan Mode or with `construction_blueprint.plan_structure("outpost", x, y)`, load the kit into Pioneer cargo, then build it. Each outpost begins with a soft capacity of **20** buildings. Expanded Outpost Infrastructure later raises every outpost's capacity by **5**. Marginal kit prices are based on founded expansion outposts plus unbuilt Outpost Kits held in physical storage: **15,000 cr**, **30,000 cr**, **50,000 cr**, **75,000 cr**, **110,000 cr**, **200,000 cr**, **350,000 cr**, **550,000 cr**, **800,000 cr**, then **1,000,000 cr** for every later kit.
researches.outpost_hub.name: Outpost Construction
researches.outpost_hub.short: Found new sites across the planet.
researches.oxygen_mk2_pack.description: Unlocks the Oxygen Generator Mk II Upgrade Pack in the shop. Retrofits a Mk I oxygen generator to Mk II for higher output.
researches.oxygen_mk2_pack.name: Oxygen Generator Mk II
researches.oxygen_mk4_pack.description: Unlocks the **Oxygen Upgrade Pack Mk IV recipe** at the Fabricator. This final tier **replaces the water input entirely** with a **Fuel Rod** magazine fed from a connected Lead Cask and draws roughly 100x Mk I power. **A generator with no rod stops producing** rather than degrading.
researches.oxygen_mk4_pack.name: Oxygen Generator Mk IV
researches.oxygen_mk4_pack.short: Nuclear-era oxygen tier, fuelled by rods.
researches.petroleum_survey.description: Unlocks survey of subsurface oil deposits and the **Oil Pump recipe**. **Deep Sonar required**: oil wells are a hidden layer for the late-tier sonar. Fabricate an Oil Pump at a Fabricator, deploy it on a surveyed well, and pipe oil to base for power generation and refining.
researches.petroleum_survey.name: Petroleum Survey
researches.petroleum_survey.short: Oil wells visible to Deep Sonar.
researches.pioneer.description: Unlocks the eight-slot Pioneer chassis in the Shop. It has no built-in battery, cargo, or Nav and cannot move until separately purchased hardware is installed.
researches.pioneer.name: Pioneer Chassis
researches.plant_terraformer.description: Unlocks the **Plant Terraformer Kit recipe** at **2,000 t Biomass**. It is the only machine that creates permanent Plants km². Feed it harvested Forage, then satisfy the cumulative phase ladder with Water, Salt, Fertilizer, and Growth Accelerant. Fabricate its kit, deploy it at an outpost, connect its supplies, and enable it from its script. Build as many as your harvest can feed.
researches.plant_terraformer.name: Plant Terraformer
researches.plant_terraformer.short: Turn harvested Forage into Plants progress.
researches.plant_terraformer_mk2.description: Unlocks the **Plant Terraformer Mk II Upgrade Pack recipe** at the Fabricator. A Mk I has no Fertilizer or Growth Accelerant injector, so it converts only up to the **Fields** threshold and then stops. Mk II adds both injectors, raises throughput from **400** to **2,200 Forage/h**, raises input feeder handling from **16** to **80 items per step**, and raises enabled draw from **180 W** to **900 W**. Each machine needs its own pack.
researches.plant_terraformer_mk2.name: Plant Terraformer Mk II
researches.pressure_mk2_pack.description: Unlocks the Pressure Generator Mk II Upgrade Pack in the shop. Retrofits a Mk I pressure generator to Mk II for higher output.
researches.pressure_mk2_pack.name: Pressure Generator Mk II
researches.pressure_mk4_pack.description: Unlocks the **Pressure Upgrade Pack Mk IV recipe** at the Fabricator. This final tier **replaces the water input entirely** with a **Fuel Rod** magazine fed from a connected Lead Cask and draws roughly 100x Mk I power. **A generator with no rod stops producing** rather than degrading.
researches.pressure_mk4_pack.name: Pressure Generator Mk IV
researches.pressure_mk4_pack.short: Nuclear-era pressure tier, fuelled by rods.
researches.prime_contractor.description: Unlocks three difficult contracts in the atmosphere-era program. Completing them contributes to Contractor Reputation; the final contract batch arrives with Smart Contractor.
researches.prime_contractor.name: Prime Contractor
researches.reservoir_engineering.description: Unlocks the **Large Liquid Tank** in the shop. It works just like a Liquid Tank, taking whatever liquid reaches it first and holding only that until it runs dry, but it holds **1,000 t** instead of 100 t. Use it where plant, essence, or wildlife supply has to ride out a long gap.
researches.reservoir_engineering.name: Large Liquid Tank
researches.reservoir_engineering.short: Holds 10× what a Liquid Tank does.
researches.rover.description: Unlocks the Rover in the Shop. Its integrated **100 Wh** battery and **10-unit** hold are fixed; Nav, Sonar, and Drill use three dedicated module slots.
researches.rover.name: Rover Chassis
researches.seed_maker.description: Opens the **Plants** tier and unlocks the **Seed Maker Kit recipe**. The machine consumes **1 t each of three different harvested life forms** to test a viable-seed recipe. Most `combine()` results have `.status == "sludge"` and produce no item; the working recipes are unique to this planet. Fabricate the kit at a Fabricator, deploy it from Inventory to an outpost, then plant the seeds you find into your Harvester field.
researches.seed_maker.name: Seed Maker
researches.shared_library.description: Adds the Library tab to the Ship Computer. Write reusable helper functions once in the Library, then import them into any machine script, so shared logic lives in one place instead of being copied everywhere.
researches.shared_library.name: Shared Library
researches.shielded_depot_ops.description: Lines every Drone Depot with containment so hot cargo can pass through your logistics network. Until this is researched a depot refuses Raw Uranium and Fuel Rods outright, and a plated drone has nowhere to unload them. Applies to every depot you own and every one you build afterwards.
researches.shielded_depot_ops.name: Shielded Depot Operations
researches.shielded_depot_ops.short: Move nuclear cargo through Drone Depots.
researches.shielded_logistics.description: Hot cargo needs a shielded lane: **Lead Casks** are the only stationary home for Raw Uranium and Fuel Rods, and **Shield Plating** lets a drone extract Raw Uranium without gaining exposure. Unlocks both items' availability; the fabrication recipes come through contractor orders.
researches.shielded_logistics.name: Shielded Logistics
researches.ship_computer.description: Unlocks the Ship → Computer page: a dashboard for system status, script management, the Playground, achievements, and notifications. Further research adds more Computer tabs, starting with the Library.
researches.ship_computer.name: Ship Computer
researches.signal_bus.description: Adds the Signal Bus tab to the Ship Computer. Scripts coordinate with each other by sending queued messages or broadcasting shared values on named channels: explicit, save-safe shared state instead of hidden globals.
researches.signal_bus.name: Signal Bus
researches.smart_contractor.description: Your Biomass recovery has opened Earth's final contractor channel. Unlocks Beat the System, Core Sample, and Lattice, the three hardest programming contracts, and completes the Contractor Reputation ladder.
researches.smart_contractor.name: Smart Contractor
researches.smelter.description: Unlocks the Smelter in the Shop. This industrial furnace reduces raw ore into refined metals and components suitable for advanced machinery.
researches.smelter.name: Ore Refinement
researches.sonar_deep.description: Unlocks the Deep Sonar module in the shop. Extends scan range to **280 m** and detects hardness-4 minerals (Neutronium) at the edge ring. Also deepens thermal/exotic survey detail and is required to reveal oil wells after **Petroleum Survey**.
researches.sonar_deep.name: Deep Sonar
researches.sonar_module.description: Unlocks Basic Sonar modules in the shop. Sonar performs point sweeps from a vehicle's current position, discovering nearby map sites and recording them in the Journal.
researches.sonar_module.name: Sonar Module
researches.sonar_wide.description: Unlocks the Wide Sonar module in the shop. Extends scan range to **180 m** and detects minerals up to hardness 3, including Titanium, Cobalt and Rare Earth, out in the mid and outer rings.
researches.sonar_wide.name: Wide Sonar
researches.sprinkler.description: Unlocks the **Sprinkler Kit recipe**. Fabricate the kit at a Fabricator, then deploy it in a Harvester field to water the four orthogonally adjacent cells (directly above, below, left, and right) while supplied. Upgrade packs improve the crops it supports.
researches.sprinkler.name: Sprinkler
researches.steam_condensation.description: Unlocks the **Steam Condenser** in the shop at **1,000,000 km² Plants**. It consumes up to **250 t/h Steam** and produces the same mass of clean Water, drawing **150 W** at full throttle. Use Gas Tanks to bridge dormant vent phases and decide how much steam becomes water instead of turbine power.
researches.steam_condensation.name: Steam Condensation
researches.steam_condensation.short: Turn vent steam into clean water.
researches.steam_tank.description: Unlocks the Gas Tank in the Shop, a passive **5000**-ton buffer that latches to the first gas it receives (steam, ammonia, swamp gas, or any gas) and holds only that gas until drained.
researches.steam_tank.name: Gas Tank
researches.steam_turbine.description: Unlocks the Steam Turbine in the Shop. At full throttle it consumes **90 t/h Steam** and produces **108 W**; a script controls the throttle.
researches.steam_turbine.name: Steam Turbine
researches.storage_bin.description: Unlocks the Storage Bin in the shop. Deployable single-material containers for stockpiling raw and refined materials at an outpost, one material per bin. Keep what you mine, stage what you need. (The Warehouse, researched later, is the larger multi-material depot.)
researches.storage_bin.name: Storage Bins
researches.thermal_cap.description: Unlocks the Thermal Cap and its **Thermal Cap Kit** recipe. Fabricate the kit at a Fabricator, then use a Constructor-equipped Pioneer to build the Cap on a surveyed thermal vent from a Planet Map blueprint. The Cap captures Steam during the vent's active phase and releases it to explicitly connected destinations; remote destinations also need a compatible completed Gas Pipe route. A chamber that reaches **100%** blows away all stored Steam, so its script must release, route, or relieve pressure. Place the blueprint in Plan Mode or with `construction_blueprint.plan_structure("thermal_cap", x, y)`.
researches.thermal_cap.name: Thermal Cap
researches.verified_contractor.description: Your terraforming output has passed Earth's vetting threshold. A second batch of contracts (denser puzzles, higher rewards) routes to your terminal. Adds new tiers to the Contractor Reputation ladder.
researches.verified_contractor.name: Verified Contractor
researches.warehouse.description: Unlocks the Warehouse in the shop. A **10,000-unit** multi-material depot: **5** material-locked slots of **2,000** each. Use it as a buffer for drone deliveries and large vehicle hauls.
researches.warehouse.name: Warehouse
researches.weather_forecasting.description: Extends new Weather Station reports and Incoming coverage from **8** to **24 world-clock hours**. Forecasts remain local to storms expected to enter powered-station coverage.
researches.weather_forecasting.name: Weather Forecasting
researches.weather_forecasting.short: See approaching storms three times further out.
researches.weather_program.description: Unlocks the **Weather Network**, installs one free completed Weather Station and its building slot at Nocturna Base, and makes additional stations available in the Shop. Observe local storms, handle live transmissions, and publish optional results to the Signal Board.
researches.weather_program.name: Weather Program
researches.wildlife.description: Opens the **Wildlife** tier and makes the **Habitat** and **Feed Maker** available in the Shop. A Habitat revives cataloged creatures and houses a breeding colony, while the Feed Maker crafts species feed from harvested **Forage** plus life forms gathered across the biomes. Hold each colony's feed, gas, and liquid bands and it breeds toward its ceiling. Gated on a thriving Plants field because every feed recipe uses Forage; harvested biome life forms provide the remaining ingredients.
researches.wildlife.name: Wildlife
researches.wildlife.short: Revive and house the first fauna.

rover_script.info:
## Overview

A programmable rover for wider planetary exploration. The chassis alone does nothing; mounted modules provide every capability. The three dedicated slots accept Nav, Sonar, and Drill modules.

Unlike the Harvester's local sector grid, the Rover travels across planet coordinates. Use `self.nav.set_target(x, y)`, set a throttle, and keep the route script running until it arrives.

## Battery

The integrated 100 Wh battery is not upgradeable. Movement, drilling, and sonar scans consume energy. High throttle is fast but less efficient. `self.battery` exposes `level()`, `wh()`, and `capacity()`. Recharge at a Vehicle Charging Station; its rescue drone can recover a stranded Rover.

## Movement lifecycle

Stopping the script, reaching its end, or hitting an uncaught error stops the Rover, clears its route, and cancels an active sonar timer. A distance tolerance only proves the Rover is close enough. Call `self.nav.brake()` after the travel loop before mining, scanning, surveying, or transferring cargo.

## Finding sites: don't roam

Every "?" contact is on the map from the start (they also block building). Instead of driving around blindly, query them: `get_component("nocturna").points_of_interest()` returns every contact with `.x`, `.y`, and a `.scanned` flag. Filter `if not p.scanned:` for your work list, drive to each contact, brake, then sweep with `self.sonar.scan()` and `survey()`. A contact's `.kind` stays `"unknown"` until you scan it: position is known from orbit, identity is not.

## Discoveries and cargo

Sonar discoveries persist in the Journal. Read them from any script with `get_component("journal").discovered_sites(planet_id)`. Mining places ore in `self.cargo`; after Auto Feeders, `self.output` can unload it to Inventory only inside the home outpost's service area, or to a Storage Bin, Warehouse, outpost machine, or stopped cargo vehicle at its current location.

Storage and outpost-machine transfers require the Rover to be inside that target's service area. Inventory is not present at remote outposts. Vehicle handoffs require both vehicles to be stopped within about 2 m.

## Modifying the rig

At any founded outpost service area, `self.modules()` shows the current layout and `self.mount(...)` / `self.unmount(...)` request dedicated-hardware service orders. Those orders may use Base Inventory for empty rig hardware, but they never make ordinary cargo available at a remote outpost. Open DOCS for `self.nav`, `self.sonar`, and `self.drill`.

Biological fieldwork is drone-only. Use a drone with a Portable Bio Scanner or Portable Bio Extractor for life-form operations.
